title: Zeta’s eyes versus the higher score

voice.direction: Independent narrator, never imitate the person pictured. Brisk upbeat conversational English, approximately 205 words per minute. Read the exact transcript only, without introductions, explanations or extra endings. Tell one connected story with natural contractions, purposeful emphasis and distinct energy between the opening, observation, score and payoff. No slow documentary voice, dramatic trailer voice, monotone list or advertising voice. Do not slow down for the product mention. Mogging.com is pronounced Mogging dot com; Clavicular is kluh-VIK-yuh-ler; Zeta is ZAY-tuh. Read digits and scores clearly. Keep pauses brief but let the visual idea land. Brisk, upbeat, conversational Orus. One narrator and one cohesive argument, with distinct energy for setup, evidence and payoff. Do not generate audio before explicit script approval.

cues.text: Look at Zeta for a second. Which feature did you notice first?

delivery.direction: Invite the viewer into a visual discovery; curious and conversational, with a small hold for the on-screen change.

visuals.reason: Show the clean full portrait without scores. Allow a brief first-look hold before the next cue; do not display the answer in captions ahead of speech.

cues.text: If it was the eyes, here's the twist: his jaw actually scores higher. The eye area gets seven point five out of ten in this Mogging portrait. The jaw gets an eight.

cues.text: But your first impression doesn't read a scorecard. The dark fringe sits close to the brows, creating a frame around the lighter eyes. That contrast makes the gaze hard to miss.
